subject.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)

question: Should OpenClaw treat every unfenced, full-line bare `<invoke name="…">…</invoke>` block as leaked tool-call content and delete it, even when it may be a legitimate XML example in an assistant reply or transcript?
rationale: The source report establishes namespaced proxy-degraded tool-call leakage, but bare XML is not intrinsically provider-owned and the PR deliberately removes it from both user-visible and persisted content. Tests cannot determine the intended product compatibility boundary.

options.title: Restrict bare-block stripping
options.body: Scrub the `antml:` and `mm:` forms plus unambiguous wrappers, while preserving bare invoke XML unless a stronger degraded-call signal exists.

options.title: Adopt strict bare-block sanitization
options.body: Accept that all full-line standalone bare invoke blocks are treated as leaked tool calls and document/test the resulting content-removal contract.

options.title: Pause for owner policy
options.body: Hold the PR until the shared-text and tool-call-repair owners decide the durable-output policy for bare XML examples.

recommendation.title: Restrict bare-block stripping
recommendation.body: Scrub the `antml:` and `mm:` forms plus unambiguous wrappers, while preserving bare invoke XML unless a stronger degraded-call signal exists.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the concrete degraded-provider reproduction and can narrow the branch once the desired compatibility rule is confirmed.
